relevance_note: Single case report of a Japanese girl with EOS/BS: 'the patient had a heterozygous c.1535A > T mutation on exon 4 in the nucleotide-binding domain of NOD2'; the Discussion also gives individual-level details of a previously published R587C mother-daughter pair [20].
method_note: Hand-extracted from the narrative text (no tables in the paper). Three in-scope people: the case-report patient ('patient'); the previously published R587C carrier from ref [20] ('ref [20] patient', sex female inferred only from 'Her daughter'); and her daughter ('daughter of ref [20] patient'), both from the Discussion with individual-level facts (onset age, features, variant). E383K and R334W are mentioned only at group level and get no rows. For the ref [20] pair the gene is not printed in the sentences about them (R587C appears in a list of EOS/BS mutations next to 'The R334W mutation in the NOD2 gene'), so gene_symbol_as_stated is 'not reported'; R587C is not in p. notation, so protein_hgvs_as_stated is null. The daughter's 'inherited maternal' rests on 'Her daughter, who had the same mutation' (mother stated to carry it). Daughter's disease label left 'not reported' ('proband of the disease'). Main patient: inheritance 'de novo' from Sanger testing of both parents, variant absent in both (paternity not addressed); variant type not stated (only 'mutation'/'transition'), so 'not reported'. ESR, CRP and MMP-3 were reported as values within the printed reference ranges, not with the word 'normal'; recorded as excluded elevated ESR/CRP/MMP-3 (D-27) and the inflammatory-marker checklist item excluded. 'Her immunological tests were normal' is a whole-investigation statement, recorded as 'abnormal immunological tests' excluded, excluding nothing more specific. Renal calcification excluded does not exclude the broader 'granulomatous nephritis or renal failure' checklist item. Age at diagnosis and age at last evaluation are not stated (presentation at 8 years; remission for over three years afterwards). The 'Additional information' section says this patient is the D512V case of reference 18 and that ref 18's report of polyarthritis and renal calcification was an error; no internal contradiction in this paper. P. acnes detection in granulomas recorded only as detail of the granulomatous dermatitis row.
